message.content:
**Columbia University** is a private Ivy League research university located in New York City, United States. Here are some key facts: | Topic | Details | |-------|---------| | **Founded** | 1754 (originally King's College) | | **Location** | Morningside Heights, Manhattan, New York City | | **Campus** | 36 acres (urban) with a mix of historic and modern buildings | | **Student Body** | ~30,000 total (≈12,000 undergraduates, ≈18,000 graduate & professional students) | | **Academic Structure** | 9 schools & colleges, including Columbia College (undergraduate), Columbia Law School, Columbia Business School, Columbia Engineering, Columbia Journalism School, and several graduate schools (e.g., Earth Institute, School of International and Public Affairs). | | **Notable Programs** | • Journalism (Columbia Journalism School) – Pulitzer‑winning faculty and alumni
• Law – one of the top law schools in the U.S.
• Medicine – Columbia University Vagelos College of Physicians & Surgeons
• Engineering – Columbia Engineering (formerly School of Mines) | | **Research** | Major research centers include the Columbia Earth Institute, the Center for Data Science, and the Columbia Genome Center. The university is a leading institution in fields such as climate science, public health, artificial intelligence, and biomedical research. | | **Rankings** | Consistently ranked among the top 10 universities worldwide (U.S. News & World Report, QS World University Rankings, Times Higher Education). | | **Alumni** | Over 100 Nobel laureates, 5 U.S. Presidents (including Theodore Roosevelt, Franklin D. Roosevelt, and Barack Obama), 2 U.N. Secretaries-General, 3 U.S. Supreme Court Justices, and many prominent figures in literature, science, business, and politics. | | **Campus Highlights** | • Low Memorial Library (iconic central library)
• Butler Library (largest academic library in the U.S.)
• Columbia University Medical Center (affiliated with NewYork‑Presbyterian Hospital)
• The Morningside Park and the surrounding neighborhood provide a vibrant urban setting. | | **Admissions** | Highly selective; acceptance rate around 6–7% (2023‑24). The university emphasizes a holistic review process, including academic record, standardized test scores (SAT/ACT optional for many programs), essays, recommendations, and extracurricular achievements. | | **Tuition & Fees** | For the 2024‑25 academic year, undergraduate tuition is approximately $68,000, with additional fees and living expenses. Columbia offers need‑based financial aid, and many students receive substantial scholarships. | | **Athletics** | Columbia Lions compete in NCAA Division I as part of the Ivy League. Popular sports include basketball, soccer, rowing, and track & field. | **Why It Matters** - **Academic Excellence**: Columbia’s rigorous curriculum and distinguished faculty attract scholars worldwide. - **Research Impact**: Its research output influences policy, technology, and global health. - **Cultural Hub**: Situated in NYC, students benefit from proximity to museums, theaters, businesses, and diverse communities. - **Alumni Network**: A powerful network that opens doors in academia, industry, government, and non‑profits. If you need more specific information—such as application deadlines, program details, or campus life—just let me know!
